newsitem.title: USA: Textron unit CEO says deal to boost 97 EPS.
newsitem.headline: Textron unit CEO says deal to boost 97 EPS.

text.p: Textron Automotive Co Chairman, President and Chief Executive John Janitz said Thursday that Textron Inc's acquisition of Kautex Werke Reinold Hagen AG, the German supplier of blow-molded plastic fuel tanks, is projected to increase its 1997 fiscal year earnings by between $0.03 and $0.04 per share.
For the 1995 fiscal year, Textron reported net income of $479 million, or $5.51 per share, on revenues of $9.97 billion.
Janitz said Textron also plans to open a new facility in Mexico in early 1997 as part of the deal for the Bonn, Germany-based Kautex, which already has 15 manufacturing facilities around the world.
"This is a new marriage where one plus one equals three," Janitz said in a telephone interview. "It adds this whole new European base" to Textron's operations.
The deal is expected to close in early January. Under the terms, Providence, R.I.-based Textron paid Klockner-Werke AG about $308 million in cash.

Kautex is the world's largest producer of plastic fuel tank systems with projected 1996 sales of about $500 million. About 63 percent of its revenues are derived from its fuel tanks, while about 18 percent are from technical automotive components.
It has manufacturing facilities in Germany, Belgium, Brazil, Canada, China, the Czech Republic, Portugal, Spain, Britain and the United States.
The new entity is to be called Kautex Textron.
The transaction is retroactive to October 1 and must still be approved by anti-trust authorities in the United States and Europe.
Kloeckner-Werke AG, the German engineering group, said the sale of its Kautex-Werke unit would cut the company's debt by 30 percent.
-- Lisa Marie Pane, New York newsdesk, 212 859-1709
